# `silk/msgpack/output`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Write MessagePack values one at a time through the ambient `Writer`.

## When to use
Use [`MsgpackOutput`](#MsgpackOutput) to write MessagePack by hand, value by value, without a tree: a scalar with
one call, an array with [`MsgpackOutput.writeArrayHeader`](#MsgpackOutput.impl.writeArrayHeader) and then its elements, a map with
[`MsgpackOutput.writeMapHeader`](#MsgpackOutput.impl.writeMapHeader) and then each key and its value. To write a tree, use
`silk.msgpack.value.Msgpack.write`. To write your own types, use
`silk.schema.msgpack.SchemaMsgpack.encode`.

## Details
Every value is written in the shortest MessagePack format that holds it: an integer from -32 to
127 takes one byte, a string of up to 31 bytes one header byte. A float is always written as a
`float 64`. Nothing is buffered and nothing is allocated; the functions do not flush the
`Writer`.

## Errors
- `MsgpackError` with `MsgpackReason.TooLong` for a length or count above 4294967295, which
  MessagePack cannot write. Nothing is written.
- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails.

## Gotchas
The functions do not check that the elements written after a header match its count. A wrong
count gives bytes that a reader misreads.

## Examples
### Write a map by hand
```silk
import silk.collections.slice { Slice }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.io.writer { Writer, WriterError }
import silk.msgpack.output { MsgpackOutput }
import silk.msgpack.scanner { MsgpackError }

struct Capture {
  bytes: [u8; 32],
  length: usize,
}

impl Writer for Capture {
  effect fn writeAll(self: &mut Self, value: &[u8]) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer {
    if self.length + value.length > 32 { fail Writer.failure() }
    Slice.copyInto<u8>(&mut self.bytes, self.length, value)
    self.length = self.length + value.length
    return ()
  }

  effect fn flush(self: &mut Self) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer { return () }
}

effect fn write() -> () ! MsgpackError | WriterError ? &mut Writer {
  // {"id": 7, "ok": true}
  run MsgpackOutput.writeMapHeader(2)
  run MsgpackOutput.writeString("id")
  run MsgpackOutput.writeUnsigned(7)
  run MsgpackOutput.writeString("ok")
  return run MsgpackOutput.writeBool(true)
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! MsgpackError | WriterError {
  let mut capture = Capture { bytes: [0; 32], length: 0 }
  run write() |> Effect.provideMut<Writer>(&mut capture)
  if Slice.view<u8>(&capture.bytes, 0, capture.length) != b"\x82\xa2id\x07\xa2ok\xc3" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="MsgpackOutput.impl.writeSigned"></a>

### Associated function `writeSigned`

```silk
pub effect fn writeSigned(value: i64) -> ()
    ! WriterError
    ? &mut Writer
```

Writes an integer in the shortest format that holds it.

#### Details

A value of 0 or more is written as [`MsgpackOutput.writeUnsigned`](#MsgpackOutput.impl.writeUnsigned) writes it, so the same
number has the same bytes whichever function wrote it. A negative value takes one byte from
-32 to -1, or `int 8`, `int 16`, `int 32` or `int 64`.

#### Errors

- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails.

<a id="MsgpackOutput.impl.writeBinary"></a>

### Associated function `writeBinary`

```silk
pub effect fn writeBinary(value: &[u8]) -> ()
    ! MsgpackError | WriterError
    ? &mut Writer
```

Writes bytes as MessagePack binary data: `bin 8`, `bin 16` or `bin 32`.

#### When to use

Use it for data that is not text. A reader tells binary data from a string, so write text
with [`MsgpackOutput.writeString`](#MsgpackOutput.impl.writeString).

#### Errors

- `MsgpackError` with `MsgpackReason.TooLong` if `value` is longer than 4294967295 bytes.
  Nothing is written.
- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails.

<a id="MsgpackOutput.impl.writeExtension"></a>

### Associated function `writeExtension`

```silk
pub effect fn writeExtension(kind: i8, data: &[u8]) -> ()
    ! MsgpackError | WriterError
    ? &mut Writer
```

Writes an extension value: the type `kind` and the payload `data`, which MessagePack does
not interpret.

#### Details

A payload of 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 bytes is written as a `fixext`, any other as `ext 8`, `ext 16`
or `ext 32`. Applications use the types 0 to 127; MessagePack reserves the negative ones,
such as -1 for a timestamp.

#### Errors

- `MsgpackError` with `MsgpackReason.TooLong` if `data` is longer than 4294967295 bytes.
  Nothing is written.
- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails.
